newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar's QAFCO considering new ammonia complex.
newsitem.headline: Qatar's QAFCO considering new ammonia complex.

text.p: Qatar Fertilizer Company Ltd (QAFCO) is considering setting up a fourth ammonia and urea complex in the Gulf state, a company official said on Tuesday.

"We are studying the proposal to set up QAFCO IV and would appoint a consultant within a month to give us an idea of the future size of the market," managing director Faisal al-Suweidi told reporters.
QAFCO already has two plants in operation with a combined output of 2,300 tonnes of ammonia and 2,500 tonnes of urea a day.
A third plant, QAFCO III, is due to come onstream later this month.
Built at a cost of $541 million, QAFCO III was designed to produce 1,500 tonnes of ammonia and 2,000 tonnes of urea a day.
"The three projects combined will make QAFCO the largest producer of fertilisers in the Middle East," al-Suweidi said.
QAFCO is 75 percent owned by the state Qatar General Petroleum Corp. and 25 percent by Norway's Norsk Hydro ASA.
